answer: Divergent Commitment Ledger. Each identity must publish a signed, evolving state commitment; a violet epoch marker advances only if the prior commitment matches. Enforcement rule: cloning one identity across agents forces identical commitments forever, so any divergence is detectable and the clone is rejected. An attacker must run a distinct full history per identity, paying synchronization and audit costs per clone rather than one seed. The lantern check verifies epoch consistency; the cipher protects commitment contents, not their uniqueness.
